article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Hybrid
Genetics: Khalifa Kush × Gastro Pop
Breeder: Khalifa Kush team
THC Content: 23–32%
CBD Content: Low to trace
Terpene Profile: Limonene , caryophyllene , linalool
Primary Flavors: Grape bubblegum, berry candy, diesel
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: early to mid-October
Indoor Yield: Moderate
Outdoor Yield: Moderate
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Point Breeze is a relatively new entry in the Khalifa Kush lineup, but its character feels deliberately connected to both old-school gas and the darker fruit-candy direction of modern cannabis. Created by crossing Khalifa Kush with Gastro Pop, the hybrid produces chunky, resin-heavy flowers with purple-tipped coloration and an aroma that can shift from grape bubblegum to unmistakable diesel within the same inhale.

The strain debuted as one of the newer creations from Wiz Khalifa and the Khalifa Kush team, and its name carries personal significance: Point Breeze references the Pittsburgh neighborhood connected to the company’s roots. Khalifa Kush describes the flower as exceptionally sticky, while current commercial batches demonstrate that the visual resin is accompanied by substantial cannabinoid and terpene production. One Florida laboratory batch, for example, measured 23.4% total THC and 2.64% total terpenes, while other retail releases have reached approximately 26% THC and 2.7% terpenes.
Genetics and Lineage

The official lineage of Point Breeze is Khalifa Kush × Gastro Pop. The Khalifa Kush side supplies the familiar fuel-forward foundation associated with the brand’s flagship weed, while Gastro Pop pulls the cross toward grape, berry candy, darker fruit, and purple flower coloration. Khalifa Kush itself was developed specifically for Wiz Khalifa in the early 2010s and remained part of his private Los Angeles stash before being released commercially. The brand now lists Point Breeze alongside Khalifa Kush, Khalifa Mints, Violet Sky, and Baby Turtle in its product library.

Gastro Pop adds a particularly important modern influence. Compound Genetics created that parent by combining Apples & Bananas with Grape Gasoline . Compound’s breeder description emphasizes blueberry-banana sweetness, skunky grape, fuel, dark purple coloration, and heavy trichome development, all characteristics that can be recognized in Point Breeze. By crossing it into Khalifa Kush, the breeding team effectively layered fruit-candy terpenes over a much more traditional gas foundation. The finished marijuana does not taste purely like either parent; grape sweetness appears immediately, yet diesel remains strong enough to keep the profile from drifting into ordinary dessert-strain territory.
Effects and Experience

The progression of the high is one of Point Breeze’s more distinctive features. The initial stage concentrates strongly around the head, with a quick cerebral elevation that can make thoughts feel lighter and surroundings more engaging. Mood may rise rapidly, conversation can flow more freely, and creative activities may become easier to sink into. Khalifa Kush describes the sensation as beginning with an elevated, almost floating head high before gradually returning the consumer toward a more grounded state that can still leave enough functional energy for the rest of the day.

That gradual descent distinguishes the hybrid from marijuana that either remains intensely stimulating or transitions immediately into couch-lock. As the session develops, the cerebral rush typically becomes calmer while a smoother physical relaxation begins to emerge. Moderate consumption may therefore work well for socializing, music, gaming, creative hobbies, or unwinding without immediately ending the evening. Potent batches deserve caution, however. Point Breeze has circulated at THC levels well into the 20% range, and some products have tested higher. Excessive consumption can produce dry mouth, red eyes, dizziness, temporary concentration problems, anxious thinking, or stronger sedation than expected, particularly for people with limited THC tolerance.
Medical Benefits

Point Breeze may interest medical marijuana consumers who prefer a cultivar that does not begin with overwhelming physical heaviness. Its combination of cerebral uplift and gradually increasing relaxation may suit patients who use cannabis while dealing with temporary stress, reduced appetite, low mood, or discomfort that makes it difficult to relax. A balanced progression can be especially desirable when someone wants relief later in the day but does not want to become immediately sleepy.

Laboratory testing also provides a more useful picture than relying solely on the strain name. One Point Breeze flower sample contained 2.64% total terpenes, led by approximately 0.84% limonene, 0.56% beta-caryophyllene, and 0.23% linalool, with humulene, pinene, ocimene, and nerolidol appearing in smaller amounts. Another commercial release similarly placed limonene, beta-caryophyllene, and linalool at the top of the profile. These compounds contribute strongly to aroma and may influence the overall cannabis experience, but Point Breeze itself has not been clinically proven to treat anxiety, depression, pain, insomnia, or any other condition. Medical consumers should use the laboratory report for their particular batch and seek professional guidance when significant health conditions or prescription medications are involved.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Grape bubblegum mixed with diesel fuel is the simplest way to describe Point Breeze, yet well-cured flower has considerably more detail beneath those two dominant notes. Breaking apart the sticky buds releases a dark berry sweetness first, sometimes resembling grape candy or fruit gum. Almost immediately, the Khalifa Kush parent pushes forward with pungent fuel. Citrus can brighten the edges of the aroma, while pepper, flowers, and subtle earth appear once the louder sweet-and-gas combination settles. Khalifa Kush specifically attributes the berry-candy component to Gastro Pop and the sharper gas character to KK.

Flavor follows the aroma closely. The opening draw can carry grape and berry sweetness before diesel builds through the middle of the palate. Limonene contributes a brighter citrus-like quality, beta-caryophyllene reinforces the dry spicy edge, and linalool can introduce a softer floral background. Instead of tasting like simple grape weed, the cultivar moves between candy and fuel, with each side preventing the other from becoming overpowering. That contrast is arguably the defining sensory characteristic of Point Breeze.
Growing Information

Khalifa Kush has not publicly released a formal cultivation sheet for Point Breeze, so precise flowering and yield figures should not be presented as breeder-established specifications. Its Gastro Pop ancestry does provide some useful context. Compound Genetics describes Gastro Pop as producing dark, heavily trichome-coated flowers capable of finishing after roughly eight weeks, with moderate internodal spacing and enough stretch to require thoughtful canopy management. Point Breeze’s finished commercial flower also shows large, rounded buds, purple coloration, and exceptionally heavy resin production, suggesting that growers working with an authenticated cut should prepare for dense flowers and substantial trichome development.

Indoors, an estimated eight-to-nine-week flowering window is a sensible starting expectation until cultivar-specific breeder data become available. Training before the canopy becomes crowded should help expose productive flowering sites to light, while selective pruning can improve air movement around the interior branches. Dense marijuana flowers demand particular attention to humidity during late bloom; trapped moisture around resinous buds can create favorable conditions for botrytis and other fungal problems.

Outdoor growers should prioritize full sun, consistent airflow, and a reasonably dry finish to the growing season. Early-to-mid-October is a practical planning estimate in many Northern Hemisphere environments, although latitude, phenotype, and the date flowering begins will determine actual maturity. Growers should ultimately rely on trichome development, flower density, and overall plant condition rather than a preset calendar date. A controlled drying environment and patient cure are especially important with Point Breeze because excessive heat or overly rapid drying can strip away the volatile grape, citrus, and fuel notes that give the cultivar its identity.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Point Breeze?

Point Breeze is Khalifa Kush × Gastro Pop. Khalifa Kush provides much of the classic gas character, while Gastro Pop contributes grape, berry-candy sweetness, purple coloration, and additional resin production.
Who bred Point Breeze?

Point Breeze was developed by Wiz Khalifa and the Khalifa Kush team. The cultivar is part of the official Khalifa Kush product family and was released as a newer addition to the brand’s strain lineup.
Is Point Breeze indica or sativa?

It is officially marketed as a hybrid rather than with a specific indica-to-sativa ratio. The effect initially feels more cerebral and uplifting before gradually settling into a calmer, more physically relaxed state.
How strong is Point Breeze?

Potency varies considerably by harvest. Current commercial examples have appeared around 23–26% THC, including a laboratory-tested batch measuring 23.4% total THC. Other releases have reached higher levels, so consumers should check the certificate of analysis attached to the particular product rather than relying on one universal number.
What does Point Breeze taste like?

The signature flavor combines grape bubblegum and berry candy with classic diesel fuel. Citrus, spice, flowers, and subtle earthy notes can appear underneath, particularly in terpene-rich batches dominated by limonene, beta-caryophyllene, and linalool.
Final Thoughts on Point Breeze

Point Breeze gives the Khalifa Kush family a distinctly modern fruit-and-gas direction without abandoning the heavy fuel character that helped define the brand. Crossing KK with Compound Genetics’ Gastro Pop brings grape bubblegum, berry candy, deep purple coloration, and abundant resin into a foundation already associated with pungent gas. The result is a visually impressive cannabis strain with a terpene profile that can exceed 2.5% in tested flower and THC potency solidly within the range experienced consumers expect from contemporary premium weed.

The effects are equally important to its identity. Rather than settling immediately into heaviness, Point Breeze begins with a pronounced cerebral lift and gradually eases toward a more grounded state. That progression gives it broader appeal than a one-dimensional sedating or stimulating hybrid. For cannabis enthusiasts who appreciate grape-forward modern genetics but still want unmistakable diesel underneath the sweetness, Point Breeze delivers a compelling combination of Khalifa Kush’s established gas profile and Gastro Pop’s darker candy-fruit character.
